title: IL-12 as the IFN-γ licensing cytokine
dek: Wikipedia's interleukin-12 page is the heterodimer from macrophages. The MSMD gene list stays on tb-host-ifng.
story: IL-12 on Wikipedia is a macrophage/dendritic-cell cytokine (p35/p40 heterodimer) that pushes lymphocytes toward IFN-γ. In TB teaching it is the upstream licence for the Th1 loop.
IL12B and IL12RB1 defects are MSMD genes on the clinic plate. This card is the ligand they concern.
IL-23 shares p40; that is why some genetic and pharmacologic stories overlap. Do not turn that sentence into a psoriasis-drug protocol here.
deep: IGRAs do not measure IL-12. They measure IFN-γ downstream.
BCG-osis in an infant with IL-12 receptor deficiency is the human knockout of this node.
Therapeutic IL-12 is not TB standard of care.
Link to wiki-ifng-glossary and wiki-th1-glossary rather than duplicating STAT1.

visual.caption: IL-12 as the licence between infected macrophage and IFN-γ. Receptor defects are the MSMD hand-off.
